contract: History import (POST /api/workflows/import/embedded-v2, EmbeddedV2ImportController) as published Server 2.11.1 serves it, in its own namespaces, from bundles built from the fixture's templates (real published exports, every ULID an order-preserving token, fixed-length ids per label, the canonical checksum and HMAC signature computed by the probe): the authentication, version, namespace, media type and JSON gates; body shapes refused as invalid_import_bundle or imported as the bundle itself; a dry run (200, estimated rows), an import (201, written rows, trimmed import_id), and repeats answered already_imported whatever their import_id; run_id conflicts with another bundle and with a native run; a tampered checksum; signatures required, unverifiable, wrong and verified; each eligibility rule (incomplete terminal history, unsupported status, missing identity, source runtime, payload codecs, memo projection, a leased task, a running attempt, and redaction, whose string paths pass as published); the request's trim and empty-to-null normalization before the checksum; bare bundles; an unparsable time that fails the write and leaves nothing; terminated, running and non-current imports; and the imported run through describe, runs, run, history and list. Bundle identities, checksums and signatures are labels; generated import ids, import times and database messages are placeholders; a ready task's wait reason is either ready form. Two published defects are bounded: the importer finds runs and instances in every namespace, so a bundle imported elsewhere answers already_imported, and an import attaches to and takes over an instance of another namespace. The published answers or the isolated ones (a run_id conflict, a refused write that leaves the other namespace unchanged) are accepted. Embedded applications have no HTTP import.
